messages:
maya: Hey team — customer on 1Password reported builds failing after they switched to our v0.3.0 tagged release. Go build error: 

samir: can you paste the exact error?

maya: sure, from their CI: 
```

go: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v0.3.0: reading https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/@v/v0.3.0.mod: 410 Gone

go: module declares its path as: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2

--- FAIL: go list -mod=mod all

```

samir: classic v2 module path mismatch. Did we change module path in go.mod but tag without /v2 suffix?

maya: customer repo imports "github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2" and their go.mod has "require github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v0.3.0" (no /v2). CI fails to resolve.

irene: that's on us — looks like the release was tagged v0.3.0 but the module path in go.mod has "/v2" so semantic import versioning requires tags v2.0.0+ (major v2 must have /v2 in module path and tags with v2 suffix).

samir: repro steps I used locally: 
1) git clone https://github.com/customer/example-app 
2) in example-app `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v0.3.0` -> fails with same message
3) editing their go.mod to `require github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2 v0.3.0` also fails because proxy expects tag v0.3.0 but module path is /v2, go proxy 410 Gone.

alex: quick mitigation: ask customer to pin to the pseudo-version from commit SHA or replace directive in their go.mod: 
```
replace github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2 => github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v0.3.0
```
That should let them build for now. Not ideal.

maya: customer needs CI green for tomorrow. Any ETA on a proper fix?

alex: engineering needs to either retag the release as v2.0.0 (or v2.0.1) with module path /v2, or publish a v0.x module without /v2 in module path. Which is intended?

irene: the API surface had breaking changes so we intended a v2. Module path in go.mod already is "module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2". We should cut a v2 tag. I can do a hotfix release workflow: retag latest commit as v2.0.0 and push to origin.

samir: note: need to push annotated tag v2.0.0 and update release notes. Also ensure GitHub release has matching tag so proxy.golang.org can fetch. After pushing tag, proxy may take a few minutes to cache.

maya: i'll relay workaround to customer and offer to apply the replace for them in their repo as temporary. Also PR to docs about Go module migration notes.

alex: one more gotcha: some customers import without /v2 in older code. We should add a small compatibility doc and examples for both import paths and show `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2@v2.0.0` usage.

devbot: release pipeline triggered: publishing tag v2.0.0 to origin by irene :rocket:

irene: pushed tag v2.0.0 and created GitHub release. CI for our SDK passed.

samir: I verified from my machine: `go list -m -json github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2@v2.0.0` returns module info now. Proxy shows v2.0.0 available.

maya: customer confirmed CI green after switching their require line to `github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2 v2.0.0` — thanks. :tada:

alex: follow-ups: (1) add a pre-release checklist for Go modules to eng-releases, (2) update SDK release notes template to remind annotating major version in tag, (3) support KB article for replace directive workarounds.

maya: logging follow-ups and closing ticket after docs update.

samir: leaving a note: if a customer can't change imports, we could also publish a v0.x module without /v2 but that's confusing. Prefer retagging for v2.

maya: resolved for now. tagging this thread for eng-releases and docs. :white_check_mark:
